contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: DELETE on an existing collection returns HTTP 200; DELETE on a non-existent collection returns 404, not 200
contract_grounding.note: The observed parameter (a never-created / already-deleted collection name) is squarely inside the assertion's constraint domain ("DELETE on a non-existent collection"), and the observed disposition is 200 — the assertion's demanded 404 — so violates=true is the honest literal reading, not a vague judgment. However the 404 half of the assertion has no textual basis on the actual v1.18.x documentation page (see doc_verification), so the violation is against the contract's asserted norm, not against prose the vendor published for this version.

chain_trace.break_detail: The contract asserts (and its endpoint_registry doc_quote repeats) that the documentation promises 404 for a non-existent collection on DELETE /collections/{name}. Direct verification of the exact source_url (HTML and .md forms) found only a 200 response documented, with a result:boolean field and no 404 branch; the in-repo OpenAPI spec for this endpoint (openapi-collections.ytt.yaml) likewise has no endpoint-specific 404, only a generic default/4XX ErrorResponse wildcard. The contract->doc link therefore rests on a doc quote that the live v1.18.x page does not contain. Links contract, script and log are intact and mutually consistent; only the doc link fails.

mundane_explanation.surviving: One vendor-side consideration cannot be excluded from source alone: the v1.18.x response schema itself documents `result: boolean` on the 200 envelope (openapi-collections.ytt.yaml delete -> response(type("boolean")), rendered on the live page), which structurally anticipates a 200+false outcome — an auditor may weigh this as an implicit idempotent-delete design affordance; however NO explicit intent evidence (no `intentionally`/`by design` comment, no maintainer citation; the only comment in the else-branch explains the create-lock, not the false-vs-NotFound choice; clone git history is depth-1 so no PR archaeology; no test pins Ok(false) as desired behavior) exists to ground by_design_in_source, so the honest source outcome remains validation_absent. Combined with the doc-layer finding (the asserted 404 promise is absent from the v1.18.x page), the adjudication hinges on whether the contract's asserted norm alone can ground a defect.
